title: API to support overlay icons on top of Task Manager apps' icons
line: Apps can now put a small overlay icon, such as a browser profile picture, on their Task Manager icon.
explanation: The Task Manager already follows the Unity launcher API (com.canonical.Unity.LauncherEntry.Update), which lets apps show a count badge, a progress bar and an urgent state on their icon, but it had no way to show an overlay icon like Windows' SetOverlayIcon. Apps therefore couldn't mark their icon with something like the active browser profile. The change reads a new "overlay-icon" key in the same signal (an icon name or a local file path/URL; other URL schemes are ignored) and shows it as an emblem in the bottom-right corner of the task icon, above the badge effect, moving to the bottom-left when the count badge sits bottom-right next to an audio indicator.

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: support overlay icons from the Unity launcher API

Apps could only show a count badge or progress on their task icons, so
there was no way to tell e.g. two browser profiles apart. Read the new
"overlay-icon" key (icon name or local file) and show it as an emblem.

BUG: 472737

media.caption: Pure master: Dolphin sends count=3 plus overlay-icon=emblem-favorite and Chrome sends overlay-icon=<avatar.png>; only the count badge appears.
With the fix: same signals; Dolphin shows the star emblem next to its badge and Chrome shows the profile avatar.
With the fix: the overlay also shows on a running Dolphin window's task.
